messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate from canary rollout (canary-id=c-42)

sam_oncall: seeing it, thanks. errors ~12% across canary nodes, latencies spiking too. paging @maria_eng and @jenna_ops

maria_eng: on it, grabbing logs. quick snapshot shows NPE in model shard init when seq_len > 2048. odd, we validated config.

sam_oncall: partial mitigation: can someone toggle the canary traffic down to 0.1? current % is 5% and is affecting customers.

jenna_ops: doing that now. /ops traffic-scale --canary c-42 --percent 0.1  // output: accepted, change in progress

deploy-bot: Canary traffic scaled: c-42 -> 0.1% by jenna_ops (reason: emergency rollback of traffic)

maria_eng: logs:
```
java.lang.NullPointerException at com.redwood.runtime.ModelShard.init(ModelShard.java:87)
config.seq_limit=4096 but runtime expects <=2048
```
Looks like the quantized variant didn't respect the seq_limit override. possible mismatch between compile flags and runtime.

sam_oncall: customers? @eric_cs can you check for customer impact / open tickets?

eric_cs: CS triage: three paying customers hit timeouts in last 10m, one reported 502s in prod. I've opened a support ticket for each and marked as high priority. sending note asking for rollback ETA.

maria_eng: quick patch idea: force seq_limit envelope at runtime to min(config, 2048) before ModelShard.init. small change, single-line guard. can build hotfix and push to canary nodes in ~12-15m.

sam_oncall: alternative is full revert of the single commit that introduced the quantization flags (commit abc1234). revert would be faster if CI passes. which is quicker?

maria_eng: revert pipeline is green-ish but running longer tests due to integration. hotfix patch has smaller surface area and fewer tests, but needs manual canary deploy. I lean hotfix.

jenna_ops: we can fast-track hotfix deploy to canary: create release tag hotfix/seqlimit-guard, build artifact, deploy to c-42 only. If that succeeds, we can lift canary % gradually.

sam_oncall: ok, proceed with hotfix path. maria, assign to yourself. jenna, standby for deploy. eric keep CS loop updated. I'll stay on call for handoff.

maria_eng: working on branch hotfix/seqlimit-guard, patch: `if (config.seq_limit > 2048) config.seq_limit = 2048;` adding unit test. pushing PR -> https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/PR/5123

jenna_ops: build kicked off by CI, watching. once artifact ready I'll deploy to canary c-42 with traffic=0.1 -> then run smoke.

incident-bot: On-call handover scheduled: sam_oncall -> maria_eng at +15m for incident continuity

jenna_ops: deploy done to canary (c-42) with hotfix tag hotfix/seqlimit-guard. smoke results: generate endpoint responding, errors down to 0.5% on canary nodes.

maria_eng: confirming logs show no NPEs on new canary nodes. running a longer 10m load test to validate.

eric_cs: CS update sent: hotfix deployed to canary; we observed immediate reduction in errors on affected customers; will update once we scale canary back up.

sam_oncall: great — once the 10m load is stable, jenna please scale canary to 2% then 10% with 5m pauses. I'll continue monitoring. If anything regresses we hit kill-switch and revert traffic to 0.

jenna_ops: scaled to 2% -> steady. scaled to 10% -> steady. overall errors returned to baseline ~0.1%.

maria_eng: pushing PR to main with hotfix and adding a guard test. will follow up with a postmortem note describing root cause: runtime/compile flag mismatch for quantized build that allowed seq_limit > supported. plan: tighten predeploy checks and add canary verification step for seq_limit distributions.

sam_oncall: handoff: I'm signing off in 10m, maria will take next oncall for this thread. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved: canary hotfix deployed, customer impact mitigated. Resolution notes: hotfix vs revert decision made; guard applied; follow-up postmortem assigned to maria_eng.
